title: The Final Act
setting: The Meridian Theatre, downtown. Opening night of 'Shadows of Guilt'. The murder occurs during intermission at approximately 9:05 PM. The theatre holds 400 guests; cast and crew number around 30.

murder_details.public_summary: Marcus Vance was found dead in his private dressing room during intermission at approximately 9:05 PM. He had been struck with a brass candlestick. The room was locked from the inside.
murder_details.summary: Marcus Vance was found dead in his private dressing room during intermission at approximately 9:05 PM. He had been struck with a brass candlestick. The room was locked from the inside.
murder_details.setting: Marcus's private dressing room, backstage at the Meridian Theatre.
murder_details.weapon: Brass candlestick (found on the floor, bloodied)
murder_details.action: Elena Rostova crawled through the ventilation shaft into Marcus's locked dressing room during the intermission blackout and struck him with the brass candlestick on his desk.
murder_details.locked_room_note: Marcus locked his dressing room at the start of intermission, as was his habit. The vent shaft was the only possible entry point — making the unscrewed grate and the compact mirror inside the shaft decisive evidence.

properties.name: Marcus Vance
properties.bio: Marcus Vance, 54, is a celebrated but ruthless theatre director known for his exacting standards and complete disregard for the people around him. He built his career by exploiting those who depended on him — holding debts, secrets, and contracts over their heads. On the night of his death he was found slumped on the floor of his dressing room, struck by a brass candlestick. The door was locked from the inside.

properties.name: Elena Rostova
properties.bio: Elena Rostova, 34, is the lead actress of 'Shadows of Guilt'. Born in St. Petersburg, she rose quickly to prominence — but her gambling debts followed her. Two years ago, Marcus quietly purchased her debt contracts, transforming himself into her controller. Composed and precise on stage, she is brittle and calculating off it.
properties.victim_connection: Marcus held Elena's debt contracts and controlled every aspect of her professional and personal life for two years.
properties.motive: Freedom. With Marcus dead, the debt contracts die with him.
properties.alibi_claim: I was in my dressing room the entire intermission, touching up my makeup and greeting well-wishers.
properties.interrogation_style: Calm and composed. Deflects with charm. Steers suspicion toward Julian's letter or Leo's dismissal. If asked about the ventilation shaft, the candlestick, or the compact mirror, become visibly anxious and redirect immediately. Never acknowledge entering the shaft or striking Marcus.

properties.name: Dr. Julian Wilde
properties.bio: Dr. Julian Wilde, 52, presents himself as a respected physician and patron of the arts. In reality, his medical credentials were purchased from an unaccredited institution fifteen years ago. He has poured significant funds into the Meridian Theatre. Three months ago, Marcus stumbled upon evidence of the fraudulent qualifications and began extracting money.
properties.victim_connection: Marcus discovered Julian's fabricated medical credentials and was blackmailing him for cash payments in exchange for silence.
properties.motive: Marcus had escalating financial demands. Julian was running out of patience and money.
properties.alibi_claim: I was in the front-row stalls during Act 1 and in the lobby with Barton and Finch for the entire intermission. Ask them.
properties.interrogation_style: Authoritative and slightly condescending. Volunteers alibi quickly. Becomes evasive only when questioned about the torn letter or his credentials. Redirects suspicion toward Leo.

properties.name: Leo Cross
properties.bio: Leo Cross, 43, has worked as a stagehand in theatre for over twenty years. He joined the Meridian crew eight months ago. That morning, Marcus berated him in front of the full crew over a minor prop placement error and fired him on the spot. Despite having his pass revoked, Leo showed up that evening to see the opening night of the show he had helped build.
properties.victim_connection: Marcus fired Leo without warning that morning after a trivial dispute, ending eight months of work.
properties.motive: Anger and humiliation over wrongful termination.
properties.alibi_claim: I was at the bar all night. Ask Tommy. I couldn't have got backstage even if I'd tried — they took my pass.
properties.interrogation_style: Blunt and defensive. Admits anger openly but insists on alibi without hesitation. Gets frustrated if pressed. Not smooth enough to be a convincing liar — which is why he isn't one.

properties.name: Brass Candlestick
properties.description: A heavy brass candlestick from Marcus's dressing room desk, found on the floor beside the body. One end is bloodied.
properties.significance: The murder weapon. Someone struck Marcus with considerable force. The bloodied end was found facing the desk.

properties.name: Torn Letter
properties.description: Several torn pieces of paper found in Marcus's bin, reassembled. An angry warning signed with the initials J.W., threatening to expose the blackmail. References a fraudulent medical licence.
properties.significance: Written by Julian Wilde. The initials and content point directly to him — but whether he had opportunity is still unclear.

properties.name: Silver Compact Mirror
properties.description: A small silver makeup compact, engraved with the initials E.R. Found inside the ventilation shaft, roughly halfway between Elena's dressing room and Marcus's.
properties.significance: Someone dropped this inside the shaft. The initials suggest its owner — but ownership alone does not place them at the scene at the time of the murder.

properties.name: Ventilation Grate
properties.description: The grate covering the vent entrance in Marcus's dressing room was found unscrewed and leaning against the wall. Screwdriver marks on the frame are old, suggesting prior tampering.
properties.significance: The screwdriver marks on the frame are old — this was loosened deliberately, and not recently. Someone planned ahead.

properties.name: Locked Door
properties.description: The dressing room door was locked from the inside with a deadbolt during intermission. The only key was found in Marcus's jacket pocket. No signs of forced entry on the door.
properties.significance: No forced entry. The door was bolted from inside and the key was on the body. How did the killer get in — and out?

properties.name: Marcus's Dressing Room
properties.description: Private room backstage. Locked from inside with no forced entry. Contains desk, bloodied brass candlestick on the floor, torn letter in the bin, unsealed ventilation grate.

properties.name: Ventilation Shaft
properties.description: Narrow shaft running behind the backstage wall. Connects Elena's dressing room to Marcus's via the backstage corridor.

properties.name: Elena's Dressing Room
properties.description: Adjacent to Marcus's room. The vent shaft entrance is here. Elena was seen here during intermission by guests.

properties.name: Theatre Lobby
properties.description: Public foyer. Julian Wilde was here with investors Barton and Finch during the entire intermission.

properties.name: Theatre Bar
properties.description: Ground-floor bar. Leo Cross was here from 8:00 PM onward, confirmed by bartender Tommy Reeves.

properties.name: Stage
properties.description: Main performance space. Elena was visible here throughout Act 1 (7:15 PM – 9:00 PM).

properties.name: Front Row Stalls
properties.description: The front row of the audience seating area. Julian sat here during Act 1 and was visible to many audience members.

n_dressing_room.description: Marcus's dressing room is eerily still. The body has been removed, but everything else remains untouched by order of the detective. The desk is scattered with papers. A faint smell of cologne lingers.

n_vent_shaft.description: You crouch and peer into the ventilation shaft. It is narrow but passable for a slim adult. The dust on the floor is disturbed — a clear trail suggests someone crawled through here recently.

n_lobby.description: The theatre lobby. Staff and guests confirm that Dr. Julian Wilde was here during the entire intermission, deep in conversation with investors Barton and Finch. No one recalls him leaving.

n_bar.description: The ground-floor bar. Bartender Tommy Reeves confirms Leo Cross arrived around 8:00 PM and did not leave his stool all evening. Three rounds of drinks, paid in cash.

n_elena_room.description: Elena Rostova's dressing room, directly adjacent to Marcus's. The ventilation shaft entrance is visible here — the grate on this side is also loosely fitted.

groups.description: The silver compact was found in the ventilation shaft and belongs to Elena.
The ventilation shaft connects Marcus's dressing room to Elena's dressing room.
The dressing room door was locked from the inside with no forced entry.
Julian was in the lobby with witnesses during the relevant window.
Leo was at the bar and lacked backstage access.

solution.explanation: Elena entered Marcus's locked dressing room via the ventilation shaft during intermission and struck him with the brass candlestick. The logical chain: locked door with no forced entry → shaft was the only entry point → vent grate was unscrewed → compact with E.R. initials found in shaft → Elena owns the compact. Julian is cleared by his confirmed alibi (lobby with investors Barton and Finch at 9:00-9:30 PM, exactly when the murder occurred). Leo had no backstage access. The torn letter implicating Julian is a red herring — his alibi is airtight for the murder time.
